## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Aparinipphannakathā* is the fifth controversy of the twenty-third chapter of the *Kathāvatthu* in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. According to the commentary and modern studies, the controversy addresses a view attributed to the Uttarāpathakas and the Hetuvādins [Dube 1980; Bareau 1955]. Basing their position on the canonical verses of the nun Vajirā—which declare that it is suffering (*dukkha*) alone that arises and ceases—these schools maintained that *dukkha* alone is determined (*parinipphanna* / *parfait*), whereas all other aggregates (*khandha*), sense spheres (*āyatana*), elements (*dhātu*), and faculties (*indriya*) are undetermined or unproduced (*aparinipphanna* / *imparfait*) [Dube 1980; Bareau 1955; Hazra 1994]. In the debate, the Theravādin interlocutor refutes this view by arguing that the scope of *parinipphanna* is not exhausted by *dukkha* proper, and because phenomena other than Nibbāna are causally conditioned (*paṭiccasamuppanna*), other constituents of mind and matter cannot be considered unproduced or uncaused [Dube 1980; Aung and Rhys Davids 1915].
SuttaCentral notes doctrinal cross-references between this text and the *Cūḷasaccaka Sutta* (MN 35), the *Kukkuḷakathā* (Kv 2.8), and the *Puggalakathā* (Kv 1.1) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus detects 165 internal Pali text-reuse matches across 17 texts, sharing extensive formulaic phrasing with other sections of the *Kathāvatthu*—most notably the *Puggalakathā* (Kv 1.1), *Indriyabaddhakathā* (Kv 17.4), *Sabbamatthītikathā* (Kv 1.6), and *Suññatākathā* (Kv 19.2)—as well as the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 1.1, Ps 3.1) and the *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus generates machine alignments with Tibetan canonical texts, such as the *Bimbisārapratyudgamana-mahāsūtra* (D 289) and *Abhiniṣkramaṇa-sūtra* (D 301), and Chinese Āgama collections (T 100, T 41) [DharmaNexus].
